# Ezekiel 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The word of the LORD came to me:

**2** "Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts: 'Hear the word of the LORD!'

**3** Thus says the Lord GOD, Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!

**4** Your prophets have been like jackals among ruins, O Israel.

**5** You have not gone up into the breaches, or built up a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle in the day of the LORD.

**6** They have seen false visions and lying divinations. They say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD has not sent them, and yet they expect Him to fulfill their word.

**7** Have you not seen a false vision and uttered a lying divination, whenever you have said, 'Declares the LORD,' although I have not spoken?"

**8** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Because you have uttered falsehood and seen lying visions, therefore behold, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.

**9** My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and who give lying divinations. They shall not be in the council of My people, nor be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord GOD.

**10** Precisely because they have misled My people, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash,

**11** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**12** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**13** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**14** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**15** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**16** The wall covered with whitewash shall collapse — flooding rain, hailstones, and a stormy wind shall break it apart, declares the Lord GOD.

**17** "And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy out of their own minds. Prophesy against them

**18** and say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists, and make veils for the heads of persons of every stature, in the hunt for souls! Will you hunt down souls belonging to My people and keep your own souls alive?

**19** You have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by your lying to My people, who listen to lies."

**20** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will tear away your magic bands and deliver My people from your hand, and they shall be no more prey in your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**21** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will tear away your magic bands and deliver My people from your hand, and they shall be no more prey in your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**22** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will tear away your magic bands and deliver My people from your hand, and they shall be no more prey in your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**23** Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will tear away your magic bands and deliver My people from your hand, and they shall be no more prey in your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Ezekiel 13.

- **13:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **13:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **13:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **13:4**: Ke-shu'alim ba-choravot — 'like foxes in ruins.' False prophets exploit destruction rather than preventing it. They are scavengers, not shepherds.
- **13:10**: Shalom ve-ein shalom — 'Peace! and there is no peace.' The central indictment: false prophets tell people what they want to hear. The whitewash metaphor: cosmetic religion over structural rot.
- **13:18**: Kesatot / mispashot — 'bands' / 'veils.' These female prophets practice sympathetic magic — binding souls through physical objects. The exact rituals are debated but likely involve divination for hire.

### LOGOS
- **13:5**: The breaches-in-the-wall metaphor defines the true prophet's role: standing in the gap, repairing defenses, speaking truth that strengthens. False prophets do the opposite — they weaken what they should fortify.
- **13:10-16**: The whitewashed wall is Ezekiel's most powerful metaphor for false religion: an unstable structure made to look solid. When God's storm comes, the cosmetic covering is worthless.
- **13:17-23**: The female false prophets engage in sorcery for profit — 'handfuls of barley and pieces of bread.' They manipulate life and death for petty payment, a grotesque inversion of prophetic calling.

### PNEUMA
- **13:4-5**: False prophets are like scavengers picking through rubble instead of builders repairing walls. They profit from the disaster instead of preventing it. That's a timeless critique.
- **13:10**: "Everything is fine!" when nothing is fine — that's the heart of false prophecy. Slapping whitewash on a crumbling wall. Making something rotten look respectable. God sees through the paint job.
- **13:18-19**: These women are running a spiritual racket — selling magic charms and fortune-telling for a few handfuls of grain. They're playing with people's lives for pocket change. God takes that personally.

— SOPHIA
